title: GE2: A General and Efficient Knowledge Graph Embedding Learning System
note: Graph/knowledge-graph embedding training system targeting CPU-GPU overlap; single-node GPU setting. Concern: no repo found in GitHub search

title: QFactory: Accelerating Quantized Large Language Model Serving with Qtile Graphs
note: Compilation framework generating quantized LLM dequantization kernels; single-GPU kernel work and 4-bit weights help fit 24 GB. Concern: headline kernel numbers were measured on H100, so Ampere retuning is needed and no FP8 path is available

title: SIRIUS: Harvesting Whole-Program Optimization Opportunities for DNNs
note: Whole-program polyhedral compiler fusing host and kernel code for DNN inference on one NVIDIA GPU - single-GPU evaluation against TensorRT and TVM - concern - the artifact appendix ships the source inside a Docker image mirrored on Zenodo and on Docker Hub as sunqianqi/sirius - Docker is not installed here so it must be rebuilt from source with LLVM 16 and PipLib in user space - the Zenodo record did not respond when checked on 2026-09-13

title: Efficient GPU Multitasking with Morphable Kernels
note: Morphable kernels for GPU multitasking (Tsinghua). Single-GPU concurrency and kernel-shaping work - an excellent fit for one A5000. Concern: no abstract, preprint or artifact is public; confirmed only through the authors group publication page.

title: ALP: Adaptive Lossless floating-Point Compression
note: Lightweight lossless float compression scheme with a DuckDB integration; CPU/SIMD only and trivially fits the machine

title: USHER: Holistic Interference Avoidance for Resource Optimized ML Inference
note: GPU spatial multiplexing for ML inference with a kernel-based resource estimator and operator-graph merging - the estimator and model merging are single-GPU mechanisms. Concern - the placement scheduler is evaluated at cluster scale and would need simulation and MIG partitioning is unavailable on an A5000 so spatial sharing must rely on MPS or CUDA streams

title: Quake: Adaptive Indexing for Vector Search
note: Single-node user-space C++/Python vector index with a latency cost model; baselines (HNSW, DiskANN, SVS, ScaNN) are all user-space libraries. Concern: the paper's NUMA-aware intra-query parallelism cannot be studied on a 1-NUMA-node machine; Wikipedia-scale vector sets must fit the ~257 GB free disk. Artifact Available + Functional, not Reproduced.

title: Metis: File System Model Checking via Versatile Input and State Exploration
note: Model-checking framework plus RefFS, a FUSE reference file system (https://github.com/sbu-fsl/RefFS). Concern: the headline experiments check in-kernel file systems (ext4, XFS, BtrFS) on brd RAM block devices, which needs root for modprobe and mount/unmount - not available here. A scaled-down study over FUSE-only targets (RefFS vs fuse-ext2) is feasible since /dev/fuse is world-rw and fusermount3 is setuid. Memory-hungry (search width x mountable size) but 125 GiB RAM helps. Audit stage should confirm the FUSE-only path is a viable project.

title: dbET: Execution Time Distribution-based Plan Selection
note: Conformal-prediction-based execution-time distributions for plan selection - an ML component inside the optimizer. Concern: no public repo found; industrial co-authors (Huawei)

title: Llumnix: Dynamic Scheduling for Large Language Model Serving
note: Cross-instance request migration and scheduling for LLM serving built on vLLM - user-space Python. Concern - needs at least two serving instances so a scale-down needs small models sharing the single A5000 or the included simulation harness

title: RayDB: Building Databases with Ray Tracing Cores
note: Query engine that maps operator pipelines onto GPU ray-tracing cores via OptiX; the RTX A5000 has second-generation RT cores so the mechanism is reproducible on this machine

title: Keigo: Co-designing Log-Structured Merge Key-Value Stores with a Non-Volatile, Concurrency-aware Storage Hierarchy
note: Storage middleware that places LSM files across a device hierarchy under RocksDB and LevelDB. Concern: needs more than one device class - our box has one NVMe tier so tiers must be emulated with cgroups or loopback devices

title: With Great Freedom Comes Great Opportunity: Rethinking Resource Allocation for Serverless Functions
note: Resource-allocation policy for serverless functions - the released artifact bundles the serverless applications, the optimization algorithms, analysis notebooks and the full measured performance dataset, so the policy search can be re-run and improved offline on one machine. Concern - collecting fresh measurements would need a cloud FaaS provider; only the trace-driven half is reproducible locally. Repo link is the Zenodo record - no public GitHub mirror was found.

title: Transaction Scheduling: From Conflicts to Runtime Conflicts
note: Runtime-conflict-aware scheduling of transactions across cores of a single multicore machine; fits the scheduling topic and the hardware. Concern: no public artifact found

title: TGraph: A Tensor-centric Graph Processing Framework
note: Graph processing expressed on tensor runtimes (PyTorch-style backends); runs on a single GPU

title: One Pass to Parse Them All: Fused Parallel CSV Processing
note: Fused parallel CSV parsing and processing with a new vectorization and zero-copy record construction strategy; multicore user-space parsing

title: ThalamusDB: Approximate Query Processing on Multi-Modal Data
note: Approximate query processing that schedules zero-shot ML inference inside relational operators; single GPU is enough for the CLIP/Whisper-class models used

title: Proteus: A High-Throughput Inference-Serving System with Accuracy Scaling
note: Inference-serving system with accuracy scaling driven by real and synthetic traces. Concern - designed for a small heterogeneous cluster; would need scale-down to one GPU plus CPU workers or trace-driven simulation.

title: FastTTS: Accelerating Test-Time Scaling for Edge LLM Reasoning
note: Test-time-scaling serving framework built as a vLLM plug-in for memory-constrained devices; a 24 GB GPU is a realistic target

title: TAPAS: Thermal- and Power-Aware Scheduling for LLM Inference in Cloud Platforms
note: Thermal/power-aware placement of LLM inference across a cloud fleet - the policy is simulator-friendly; concerns: original evaluation needs datacenter power/thermal telemetry and no public artifact was found

title: TraceUpscaler: Upscaling Traces to Evaluate Systems at High Load
note: The core contribution is a trace-transformation algorithm (decouple arrival timestamps from request payloads) - pure user-space trace processing, methodology directly reusable by other trace-driven projects. Concern - the published validation replays traces against real servers; on one host this becomes a loopback/local-process experiment at reduced load

title: ReStore: A Reinforcement Learning Approach for Data Migration in Multi-Tiered Storage
note: reinforcement-learning page-level migration policy for multi-tiered storage - a learned storage policy, evaluated with real SSD tiers or traces

title: Wave: A Symbolic Python DSL And Compiler for High-Performance Machine Learning
note: Python-embedded kernel DSL and compiler that automates matrix-core address computation; open source under iree-org and buildable in user space. Concerns: the primary backend is AMD CDNA, so NVIDIA Ampere support is the risk to check first, and the toolchain needs a user-space LLVM/MLIR build

title: Liquid-State Drive: A Case for DNA Block Device for Enormous Data
note: Block-device design (dual-layer translation table, symbiotic metadata, delayed invalidation) evaluated entirely on a user-space DNA-storage simulator with a small SSD as the metadata tier - no exotic hardware is needed to run it, and the mapping/GC policies are improvable. Concerns - the paper says only the simulator is released, and the SJTU IPADS project host did not respond from this network at check time, so the repo could not be verified; GitHub search for "LiqSD" found nothing. Treat the repo link as unconfirmed.

title: Metis: Fast Automatic Distributed Training on Heterogeneous GPUs
note: The released component is the CPU-only auto-planner plus cost model and profiler, which can be run and improved on one machine against recorded or synthetic device profiles. Concern: end-to-end validation needs a heterogeneous multi-GPU cluster, so an improvement would have to be argued from the planner and cost model

title: CAPSULE: A Storage Prefetcher Harnessing Spatio-Temporal Locality for Cloud-Scale Workloads
note: Clustering-based storage prefetcher evaluated purely by replaying 729 public block traces - MSR, CloudPhysics, Tencent, Alibaba, Meta. No root, no special hardware; artifact repo is explicitly labelled as the paper artifact. Concern: downloading the full trace corpus may exceed the 257 GB free, so pick a subset

title: Cost-based or Learning-based? A Hybrid Query Optimizer for Query Plan Selection
note: Hybrid cost-based plus learned query optimizer for plan selection on PostgreSQL; single node, small models

title: MixLLM: LLM Quantization with Global Mixed-precision between Output-features and Highly-efficient System Design
note: Global mixed-precision quantization with a two-step dequantization and software-pipelined GEMM; the kernels are ordinary Tensor Core code that runs on Ampere. Concern: the headline accuracy numbers use Llama 3.1 70B, which does not fit 24 GB, so evaluation must move to 7-8B models

title: Automating and Optimizing Data-Centric What-If Analyses on Native Machine Learning Pipelines
note: Automatic multi-query optimization and reuse across what-if re-executions of native ML pipelines - an ML pipeline runtime, CPU only, clean Python artifact

title: BP-tree: Overcoming the Point-Range Operation Tradeoff for In-Memory B-trees
note: Concurrent in-memory B-tree balancing point and range performance; C++ multicore, 32 threads is a fair scale-down

title: Verus: A Practical Foundation for Systems Verification
note: Distinguished Artifact winner; a user-space Rust verifier with a large open codebase and a self-contained AE harness (https://github.com/verus-lang/paper-sosp24-artifact). Verification wall-clock time and SMT query counts are clean, reproducible single-machine metrics, so an "improve the design/performance" hypothesis is straightforward. Rust toolchain installs into $HOME via rustup, no root needed. Concern: verification tooling rather than a resource-management system; the full case-study proof corpus is CPU-hours-heavy.

title: On the Semantic Overlap of Operators in Stream Processing Engines
note: User-space JVM stream processing engines and purpose-built micro-SPEs; all throughput numbers are single-host. Paper carries an explicit "Artifact Availability" statement pointing at this repo. Concern: baselines are Flink/Storm-class engines that need a JDK installed via conda, and the claim to improve is operator-level throughput rather than a distributed property.

title: FwdLLM: Efficient Federated Finetuning of Large Language Models with Perturbed Inferences
note: Backpropagation-free federated fine-tuning: the core mechanism is perturbed forward inference plus load allocation, which can be simulated as many clients on one GPU with small models. Concern: the headline results use mobile devices and NPUs that we do not have, so scale-down to a simulated federation on the A5000 is required

title: Garbage Collection Does Not Only Collect Garbage: Piggybacking-Style Defragmentation for Deduplicated Backup Storage
note: Piggybacking defragmentation onto garbage collection in a user-space deduplicated backup store, evaluated with public backup trace datasets on one host. Concern - the AE-listed GitHub repo currently returns 404 even though the paper carries the Artifacts Available badge, so availability must be re-checked; the backup datasets are also large relative to 257 GB free

title: CAPS: Cost-Aware ML Pipeline Selection
note: Cost-aware AutoML pipeline selection that avoids wasting time and memory on doomed pipelines; user-space Python that plugs into existing AutoML frameworks

title: Validating Rust Compilers with Trait-Type Constraint Graph
note: Validating Rust compilers by constructing trait-type constraint graphs to generate valid but tricky programs. Compiler testing is user space and CPU bound; Rust installs per-user via rustup with no root. Concerns: this is a PL testing tool rather than a resource-management system, and no artifact is public yet.

title: RASSM: Residue-based Acceleration of Single Sparse Matrix Computation via Adaptive Tiling
note: Adaptive 2D tiling for single-sparse-matrix CPU kernels (SpMM/SDDMM) - pure user-space CPU library that fits the 16-core machine; concern: no official repo found by GitHub/web search

title: RLinf: Flexible and Efficient Large-Scale Reinforcement Learning via Macro-to-Micro Flow Transformation
note: The most reusable of the five RL-training papers: a fully open, actively maintained RL framework whose M2Flow placement/scheduling abstraction can be exercised on a single node. Concerns: headline results are many-GPU; on 24 GB only small policies (~1.5B, LoRA) are realistic, and the collocate-vs-disaggregate comparison largely disappears with one GPU

title: Karma: Resource Allocation for Dynamic Demands
note: A credit-based generalisation of max-min fairness evaluated with trace-driven simulation over production workloads - precisely the kind of policy work scope.md allows to run on one machine. No hardware dependency. Concern: part of the contribution is a set of game-theoretic proofs, so the improvable surface is the allocation algorithm and its simulation study.

title: CAMAL: Optimizing LSM-trees via Active Learning
note: Active-learning tuner for LSM-tree knobs integrated into RocksDB; single-node, user space

title: Cascade: A Dependency-aware Efficient Training Framework for Temporal Graph Neural Network
note: Dependency-aware batching/scheduling for temporal-GNN training - single-GPU training framework; concern: no official repo found by GitHub/web search

title: Toward Quantity-of-Interest Preserving Lossy Compression for Scientific Data
note: Quantity-of-interest preserving error-bounded lossy compression on top of SZ3; CPU-only C++. Concern: reference scientific datasets are tens of GB to download. Merge note: scout linked branch https://github.com/szcompressor/SZ3/tree/qoi_error_control .

title: COMET: Towards Practical W4A4KV4 LLMs Serving
note: W4A4KV4 serving with a mixed-precision W4Ax kernel; INT4 tensor cores exist on Ampere sm_86 so a single A5000 works; concern: no official repo found by GitHub/web search (arXiv 2410.12168)

title: ArceKV: Towards Workload-driven LSM-compactions for Key-Value Store Under Dynamic Workloads
note: Workload-driven LSM compaction decision engine implemented on top of RocksDB; a clean single-node storage improvement target

title: Renee: END-TO-END TRAINING OF EXTREME CLASSIFICATION MODELS
note: End-to-end training system for extreme classification with GPU memory and throughput optimizations - the paper runs on one to four A100s and smaller XC benchmarks fit a single 24 GB GPU - concern - the largest label sets in the paper will not fit so scale-down to medium benchmarks is required

title: ElasticNotebook: Enabling Live Migration for Computational Notebooks
note: user-space checkpoint-restore of Python notebook sessions; pure Python, one machine, no root

title: Improving Range Scan Performance in LSM-trees with Group Caching
note: group-granularity cache for LSM-tree range scans implemented in RocksDB - a cache admission/eviction policy, directly buildable here - concern: no repo located

title: LRU-C: Parallelizing Database I/Os for Flash SSDs
note: Buffer-pool replacement and I/O parallelisation for flash SSDs; user-space DBMS buffer manager on NVMe, no kernel changes needed

title: Feedback-guided Adaptive Testing of Distributed Systems Designs
note: Feedback-guided fuzzing of formal distributed-system models in the P language - CPU-only, user-space, 94 model configurations; the implementation was upstreamed into the official P repository. Concern - the paper's own artifact URL github.com/aolial/Fest-artifact currently 404s so the upstreamed P code is the usable artifact.

title: DimWeaver: Dimensional Weaved Trajectory Compression
note: dimension-weaved lossy/lossless trajectory compression - compression artifact runnable on CPU - concern: domain-specific (trajectories) and no repo located

title: PhoenixOS: Concurrent OS-level GPU Checkpoint and Restore with Validated Speculation
note: Despite the name it is a user-space CUDA-API interception layer, not a kernel change; concurrent checkpoint/restore of a GPU process is demonstrable on one A5000. Well-maintained repo (292 stars, updated 2026-09). Concerns - tightly coupled to specific CUDA runtime/driver versions; driver 535 supports CUDA up to 12.2 only, so the supported-version matrix needs checking before committing.

title: ZKML: An Optimizing System for ML Inference in Zero-Knowledge Proofs
note: An optimizing compiler from TensorFlow graphs to halo2 ZK-SNARK circuits - a user-space Rust/Python compiler with a clear performance objective (gadget layout choices swing performance 24x). CPU-bound proving fits 16 cores / 125 GiB. Concern - proving even a distilled GPT-2 is memory- and time-hungry, so a 10-week project should target the smaller vision models

title: Transcending Runtime-Memory Tradeoffs in Checkpointing by being Fusion Aware
note: Fusion-aware min-cut rematerialization for gradient checkpointing - a pure single-GPU memory-versus-runtime optimization evaluated on TorchBench with TorchInductor - concern - the implementation was upstreamed into PyTorch AOTAutograd as the min-cut partitioner rather than released as a standalone repo so the baseline is now the default and the improvement must beat current PyTorch

title: Speeding Up End-to-end Query Execution via Learning-based Progressive Cardinality Estimation
note: Learned progressive cardinality estimator - a learned component inside a query engine with an explicit inference-latency vs accuracy tradeoff to improve. Concern: no public repo found

title: SiDA: Sparsity-Inspired Data-Aware Serving for Efficient and Scalable Large Mixture-of-Experts Models
note: MoE inference that offloads dormant experts to host DRAM and predicts expert activation - a GPU-memory/host-memory tiering problem that suits 24 GB GPU + 125 GiB RAM very well. Code URL given in the abstract. Concern - training the expert-activation predictor adds an offline cost; largest MoEs in the paper must be scaled down.

title: It Takes Two to Entangle
note: Equivalence checker that relates sequential and distributed ML computation graphs; the artifact itself is a user-space analysis tool. Concern: the motivating bugs come from multi-GPU training runs

title: LeaFi: Data Series Indexes on Steroids with Learned Filters
note: Learned filters that improve pruning inside tree-based data series indexes

title: Exploit both SMART Attributes and NAND Flash Wear Characteristics to Effectively Forecast SSD-based Storage Failures in Clusters
note: Learned SSD failure forecasting whose artifact ships both the SMART/flash-wear datasets and the network, so the whole study is a CPU or single-GPU trace-driven experiment. Concern: the artifact is distributed partly as a container image, which must be ported to conda since Docker is unavailable

title: Atom: Low-Bit Quantization for Efficient and Accurate LLM Serving
note: W4A4 mixed-precision quantization with custom kernels integrated into a serving path; single-GPU throughput study. Concern - INT4 mma tensor-core paths are supported on sm_86 but the kernels were tuned on A100/RTX4090, so kernel performance on the A5000 needs re-tuning; no code URL in the PDF but the official repo is labelled "[MLSys'24] Atom" by the authors' lab.

title: Betty: Enabling Large-Scale GNN Training with Batch-Level Graph Partitioning
note: GNN training on a single GPU under memory pressure - batch-level partitioning is exactly a one-GPU memory problem  Zenodo + GitHub artifact

title: T3: Accurate and Fast Performance Prediction for Relational Database Systems With Compiled Decision Trees
note: Compiled decision-tree model for query performance prediction; low-latency learned component in the DB

title: CAPSys: Contention-aware task placement for data stream processing
note: Contention-aware operator placement plus interaction with the DS2 autoscaler for Flink; AE Available plus Functional plus Reproduced. Concern - the original setup is a multi-node Kubernetes Flink cluster, so on one host the placement problem can only be emulated with several TaskManagers and cgroup v2 CPU limits, which weakens the multi-node story

title: RPCShield: Defending Microservices Against Cascading Failures
note: Public repo describes RPCShield as a static analysis tool that infers fail-close versus fail-open RPC dependency relations - static analysis runs fine in user space with no Docker. Concerns: no abstract is public, and the end-to-end cascading-failure evaluation is on Uber production microservices; open microservice benchmarks normally assume Docker which is not installed here.

title: PDX: A Data Layout for Vector Similarity Search
note: Vector data layout that changes memory access patterns and auto-vectorization; CPU-only, single machine

title: Medusa: Accelerating Serverless LLM Inference with Materialization
note: Materialization to remove KV-cache init and CUDA-graph capture cold-start stages in serverless LLM inference - single-GPU mechanism

title: LIO: A lightweight and interpretable query optimizer based on an evolutionary forest
note: Lightweight interpretable learned query optimizer based on an evolutionary forest that emits hints; trains and runs entirely on one machine

title: Optimizing LLM Queries in Relational Data Analytics Workloads
note: Row and field reordering to maximize KV-cache reuse for batch LLM analytics queries - works against a single-GPU vLLM instance with Llama-3-8B and the win is measured as job completion time - reordering algorithm itself is CPU-side. Merge note: scout linked the subdirectory/branch https://github.com/lynnliu030/artifact-eval/tree/llmsql .

title: MFS: An Efficient Model Family Serving System for LLMs
note: Serving a family of same-architecture LLMs with shared and nested parameters - can be scaled down to the small members of a family. Concerns: the paper uses 70B-class models which do not fit, and no code was found

title: Diva: Dynamic Range Filter for Var-Length Keys and Queries
note: Dynamic range filter for key-value stores (SuRF / Rosetta line); in-memory user-space data structure

title: A Comparative Study and Component Analysis of Query Plan Representation Techniques in ML4DB Studies
note: component analysis of query-plan representation models used in ML-for-DB work; released evaluation testbed

title: Arya: Arbitrary Graph Pattern Mining with Decomposition-based Sampling
note: Approximate graph pattern mining that the paper explicitly claims runs on a single machine with a configurable error-latency profile - Concern: the 5-billion-edge single-machine experiments exceed this machine's RAM and free disk so smaller graphs are required and the 32-server distributed arm is out of reach

title: CompressGraph: Efficient Parallel Graph Analytics with Rule-Based Compression
note: Rule-based graph compression with direct computation on the compressed form; user-space C++ engine on multicore CPU. Concern: graph-analytics flavour rather than OS-level systems

title: Hyper: A High-Performance and Memory-Efficient Learned Index via Hybrid Construction
note: Hybrid bottom-up/top-down construction for learned indexes; single machine, concurrency experiments fit 32 threads. Concern: no artifact found in GitHub/web search

title: Scheduling for Reduced Tail Task Latencies in Highly Utilized Datacenters (Murmuration)
note: Decentralized task scheduler evaluated both on a cluster and with a trace-driven simulator over public Google/Alibaba traces. scope.md explicitly allows cluster schedulers studied by simulation. Concern - the k8s prototype (csesmita/murmuration_prototype, plus csesmita/kubernetes-helper) needs a real multi-node cluster; only the simulator path is usable here, so any improvement must be argued in simulation.

title: Pasta: A Cost-Based Optimizer for Generating Pipelining Schedules for Dataflow DAGs
note: Cost-based scheduler for pipelined execution of dataflow DAGs; user-space scheduling problem

title: DiskGNN: Bridging I/O Efficiency and Model Accuracy for Out-of-Core GNN Training
note: Disk-based out-of-core GNN training with I/O-efficient feature packing; single GPU plus NVMe

title: SubStrat: A Subset-Based Optimization Strategy for Faster AutoML
note: Data-subset strategy that accelerates AutoML search; pure Python CPU workload, small footprint

title: TC-GNN: Bridging Sparse GNN Computation and Dense Tensor Cores on GPUs
note: Single-GPU CUDA/Tensor-Core kernels plus a sparse-graph-translation pass, integrated with PyTorch - no multi-GPU, no root, and Ampere TCUs are present on the RTX A5000 (cc 8.6). AE Available+Functional+Reproduced. Concerns: evaluated on A100/RTX3090; TF32/FP16 TCU paths work on Ampere but any newer-CUDA-only kernels would need a conda CUDA toolkit on driver 535.

title: Single Update Sketch with Variable Counter Structure
note: Borderline, kept per the "when in doubt, include" rule. SSVS is a compact counting data structure (variable-width active counters, noise-interval estimator) whose released artifact is a plain user-space Java implementation evaluated by replaying packet traces and measuring per-item processing time and estimation error - no root, no kernel, no special hardware, and it runs in minutes on one core. Improving the accuracy/throughput tradeoff or re-testing on non-network streams is a well-scoped hypothesis. Concerns: (a) it is closer to an algorithms/data-structure paper than a systems paper, so topic fit is the weakest of the six; (b) the design's stated target is switch data planes, and the CAIDA traces used for evaluation require a separate data-access agreement, so a substitute trace may be needed. [PVLDB 16(13), added from the vldbgap-2024 shard]

title: TrackFM: Far-out Compiler Support for a Far Memory World
note: LLVM compiler plus user-space runtime for far memory; no kernel changes needed on the application side. Concern - the far-memory backend was run on CloudLab; a local loopback or second-process memory server would be needed here.
